notes: Forest, thicket and estuary birds of the Garden Route (Wilderness, Knysna, Tsitsikamma, Plettenberg Bay), Hogsback and the Amathole forests, the Eastern Cape thicket (Addo) and the Wild Coast (Port St Johns), which the country trip does not hold. Hand-picked from the species list of South Africa with GBIF/eBird record counts (occurrence.csv) and birding knowledge. Left out as vagrants or hard to tell apart in photos: Forest Buzzard, African Barred Owlet, African Dusky and Ashy Flycatchers, the three cuckoos Black, African and Levaillant's, Yellow-streaked Greenbul, Rufous-chested Swallow, Red-winged Francolin and the swifts. The other South Africa packs were being written at the same time and had already claimed most birds of this coast belt (ZA-NATAL took nearly all the eastern forest birds, ZA-FYNBOS the seabirds and forest raptors, ZA-KAROO the arid birds of the Karoo edge such as Black-headed Canary, Pale-winged Starling and Karoo Long-billed Lark, ZA-LOWVELD Bearded Scrub Robin and Southern Brown-throated Weaver, both left to it although they are also birds of Addo and the Wilderness lakes). ZA-NATAL had claimed many of the forest birds kept here when this pack was written, and no longer lists any of them, so no bird sits in two packs. Algoa Bay seabirds (Black-browed and Indian Yellow-nosed Albatross, Sooty and Great Shearwater, White-chinned Petrel, Brown Skua, Northern Giant-Petrel) are in ZA-FYNBOS, not here. Photo picks were made by hand from contact sheets of the local library; Cape Parrot, Knysna Warbler, Barratt's Warbler and Crowned Eagle photos are weak and flagged for review. No bird was dropped for lack of photos. 28 species.
